evidence: Static row; judged by reading the frozen brief and the six notes, no runtime evidence is needed or claimed. instruction.md is three short first-person paragraphs with a contraction, a personal habit and varied sentence length: instruction.md:1 "I'd like a small local playground ... I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source." and instruction.md:5 "I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in." A grep over instruction.md and all six notes for marketing gloss (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, comprehensive, intuitive, ensure, utilize, powerful, elegant), em dashes, bullets and numbered lists returned no match; every note is plain prose paragraphs under one short heading. The notes keep the same speaker: overview.md:3 "while I work", ui.md:3 "Don't use a textarea ... as long as the source I see is drawn by your own surface", behaviour.md:11 "That refresh must not touch what I'm doing ... say so and keep my draft". Cadence varies, including short sentences among long ones: ui.md:11 "Navigation wraps at the ends.", security.md:5 "Save source as text.", behaviour.md:13 "History inspection is read-only.", policy.md:3 "A parser or formatter library is fine". Weaker points, neither amounting to the defect in quality-checks.md:15: (a) the speaker is "I" everywhere except integration.md:1 and integration.md:3 ("How we start the app", "We start it with node /app/server.js"), a small I/we shift inside a note that is otherwise the operator's runtime description; (b) ui.md:5-17 and behaviour.md:3-13 are long, dense paragraphs with a heavy share of "must" (6 in behaviour.md, 4 in ui.md), so they read as a careful specification written by a person rather than as casual notes. That density is a matter for row 1 and the scope rows; the wording itself is plain, concrete and not over-polished. The template supplies only CHANGE_ME placeholders for instruction.md and notes.md, so the voice is entirely task-authored and no template text is at issue.
